articles.title: How to Build a Claude‑Powered RAG Chatbot Over Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL, Explained Simply
articles.excerpt: You can’t rely on a flat vector store when your data lives in relational tables. By the end of this guide you’ll have a live Node.js service that pulls context from Aurora Serverless v2, crafts a prom…
articles.body: You can’t rely on a flat vector store when your data lives in relational tables. By the end of this guide you’ll have a live Node.js service that pulls context from Aurora Serverless v2, crafts a prompt, and lets Claude answer like it’s reading the docs straight from your database. Why RAG Needs a Real Database, Not Just a Vector Store RAG – short for Retrieval‑Augmented Generation – is the pattern of first looking up relevant information and then feeding it to a language model so the answer is grounded in reality. In plain English: RAG is like asking a friend to look up a fact in a cookbook before they reply to your dinner‑question. A vector store holds dense numeric representations (vectors) of text and lets you find “similar” items quickly.

articles.title: Is This Selfie a Profile or a Three-Quarter View? A Python Face-Yaw Check Before a Malfoid AI Upload
articles.excerpt: Is This Selfie a Profile or a Three-Quarter View? A Python Face-Yaw Check Before a Malfoid AI Upload The photo-requirements guide for Malfoid AI asks for one clear, front-facing photo of one adult, wi…
articles.body: Is This Selfie a Profile or a Three-Quarter View? A Python Face-Yaw Check Before a Malfoid AI Upload The photo-requirements guide for Malfoid AI asks for one clear, front-facing photo of one adult, with the whole face visible. The good/bad table on that page is blunt: "Facing the camera, eyes open" versus "Profile shots and faces turned far away." A file can still contain a face and fail that test. The head is turned. You see one ear clearly and the far eye is almost gone. That is yaw — left/right head turn — not tilt, and not a small face in a wide room. This is a pre-upload check for that case. It is not a roll or leveling check (I wrote one of those on 14 November, using YuNet and a symmetry measure of tilt).

articles.title: Payment Failed? Why 1 in 6 Shoppers Quit at Checkout
articles.excerpt: A customer finds your product, adds it to the cart, taps Pay, and gets this: ❌ Payment failed. Your payment couldn't be processed. No reason. No next step. Just a red box and a "Try again" button that…
articles.body: A customer finds your product, adds it to the cart, taps Pay , and gets this: ❌ Payment failed. Your payment couldn't be processed. No reason. No next step. Just a red box and a "Try again" button that usually fails the same way. Most of the time, the customer doesn't try again. They close the tab. I'm Zubair Hussain , an AI engineer and full-stack developer. I've spent a lot of time debugging checkouts, and the pattern is always the same: the sale isn't lost because of the product. It's lost in the few seconds between "I want this" and "payment confirmed." Here's what actually goes wrong in that gap, and what I ship to fix it. TL;DR About 1 in 6 U.S. shoppers have abandoned an order because checkout was too long or complicated.

articles.title: rclone's Extended-Attribute Writes Could Escape the Destination Root
articles.excerpt: rclone's Extended-Attribute Writes Could Escape the Destination Root rclone is often used to copy files and preserve metadata across storage systems. CVE-2026-134354 shows a metadata feature bringing…
articles.body: rclone's Extended-Attribute Writes Could Escape the Destination Root rclone is often used to copy files and preserve metadata across storage systems. CVE-2026-134354 shows a metadata feature bringing its own path risk. The advisory says the local backend's setXattr function could follow a planted symbolic link and write user.* extended attributes to a file outside the destination root. The issue requires --links and metadata operations, according to the published description. An attacker who can place a symlink in the destination tree and arrange for an outside directory to contain a child with the relevant name can influence that outside file's extended attributes. Why metadata writes matter Extended attributes carry labels, user metadata and application-specific state.

articles.title: 0xC00D36C4 Error: Why Windows Won't Play Your Video (and the Free Fix)
articles.excerpt: Windows hands back 0xC00D36C4 when its player can't decode what's inside your file — not because the file is broken. The container opens, the metadata reads fine, and then the player hits a video stre…
articles.body: Windows hands back 0xC00D36C4 when its player can't decode what's inside your file — not because the file is broken. The container opens, the metadata reads fine, and then the player hits a video stream no installed decoder claims, giving up with a hex code. Most of the time that stream is HEVC: the codec your phone has saved by default since iOS 11, and the one Windows sells back to you for $0.99. Here's what the error actually signals, five fixes ranked by what they really cost, and the one that makes the file itself play everywhere. Convert HEVC to H.264 locally — no upload → H.264 output, runs in your browser, nothing uploads. Files up to 500 MB. Free — unlimited uses, no sign-up.

articles.body: A custom Playwright reporter takes about 26 lines, but the obvious way to count failures in it is wrong. On a 13-test suite with 2 failing tests, a reporter that counted failed results in onTestEnd reported 8 failures, in 5 of 5 runs. I wrote a minimal reporter, then measured four places where the reporter API does not do what a first version expects. The reporters, the seeded suite and the raw output of every run are in the PoC repo . The suite 13 tests against a small cart page built in the test file. 8 pass, 2 always fail, 2 fail on the first attempt and pass on retry, 1 is skipped. retries: 2 , workers: 4 , fullyParallel: true . Playwright 1.65.1 with Chromium, Node v24.14.1, macOS on arm64.

articles.body: A percentage-of-spend fee pays the manager more when you spend more, whether or not your results improve. That is the whole argument. The rest is when it matters and what to ask so you can tell. If you are paying for Google Ads management as a share of your ad budget, or you are about to, this is not an accusation against the person on the other side. The point is narrower: the fee structure has a built-in lean, and you are the one who has to know which way it leans. What a Percentage-of-Spend Fee Actually Pays For Take a simple case. You spend €5,000 a month on ads and the manager takes a fixed share of that. The next month you spend €10,000. Nothing about the work has to change for the fee to double. Same account, same campaigns, same weekly check-in – twice the invoice. Now flip it.

articles.excerpt: Three stars, 28 light-years, and one big cosmic mystery.
articles.body: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour.

articles.title: Ariane 6 launch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites postponed due to a technical issue
articles.excerpt: The next launch attempt will be no earlier than Nov. 24.
articles.body: Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft has been postponed due to a technical issue. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation was scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Monday (Nov. 23). However, the countdown was halted following a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace . The countdown was stopped before the removal of the mobile gantry, with Arianespace confirming that the rocket and its satellite payload remain safe and stable. Technical teams are now assessing the issue, with the next launch opportunity no earlier than Tuesday (Nov. 24).
